subject: Post-call: Streamline Health — inference cost pressure & pilot readout
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jenna Harris <jenna.harris@streamlinehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Streamline Health — inference cost pressure & pilot readout

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Below is a short, actionable recap so we have alignment on pain, goals, constraints, and next steps for a lightweight pilot. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Key pain points you shared
- Token costs increasing dramatically as usage scaled; current monthly inference spend growing ~2.5x YoY with bursty traffic.
- Tail latency during morning peak causing ~15% increase in user-facing timeouts (p95 spikes).
- Ops overhead: your SRE team is spending cycles on autoscaler tuning and retry policies to avoid failures when model containers evict.

Current stack (as stated)
- Serving: self-hosted K8s cluster with CPU fallbacks + occasional GPU pool for nighttime exports.
- Cache: Redis used for some partial-result caching; no integrated KV prefix caching for model KV.
- Models: mixture of open 7B and 13B variants (internal forks), runs are mostly fp16 on GPU and CPU fallback in production.

Success criteria for a pilot (what would make this successful)
- Unit economics: reduce inference cost per 1k tokens by >=60% (or show clear path to it with config changes).
- Latency: p95 tail < 250ms for interactive calls under stated traffic shape.
- Quality guardrails: no more than 2% relative degradation on your eval set (we'll use your prompt set + our regression harness).

Openness to techniques
- Batching & caching: you indicated willingness to accept batching up to ~50ms extra per-request when amortized if it brings cost benefit; very interested in prefix and KV cache for repetitive prompts.
- Quantization: acceptable to pilot INT4/4-bit quant if we can run a quick regression and rollback on quality.

Proposed pilot scope (4 weeks)
- Week 0: exchange traffic shape, sample prompts, and baseline traces (you -> provide anonymized slice of production).
- Week 1: Redwood runs benchmarking on a staged copy: batching strategies + prefix/KV caching tests.
- Week 2: deploy a shadow pilot against ~5% traffic (non-blocking); measure cost and latency.
- Week 3: evaluate results, tune quantization profile; present report and recommended production config.

Immediate asks from your side
1) Share a sanitized sample of: 1M token-day traffic shape, 10 representative prompts, and current p95/p99 traces (anonymized).
2) Confirm regulatory constraint: PHI in payloads? (you mentioned some clinical notes — want to confirm).

Next meeting proposal
- 30 min sync next Tue 28 Apr at 10am PT to finalize MOP and scope. If that doesn't work, propose a slot and we'll accommodate.

Attachments: pilot-scope-template.xlsx (blank fields for traffic shape), current-usage-snapshot.csv (what we asked for)

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Jenna Harris <jenna.harris@streamlinehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Alex Moore <alex.moore@streamlinehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:02:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Streamline Health — inference cost pressure & pilot readout

Thanks Karthik — this is a great tidy recap. A few clarifications/notes from our side: 

Clarifications
- Regulatory: yes, we do handle PHI in some flows; any pilot that touches real data will need a reviewed NDA + SOC2 artifacts. For the initial benchmarking you can use anonymized low-sensitivity slices — we'll provide those.
- On quantization: our ML team is open to INT4 testing but will want to see the regression harness results first; we cannot accept >2% drop on our clinical retrieval accuracy metric.
- Cache expectations: we get a lot of repeated prefixes in our triage workflow; TTL-based prefix caching sounds promising. Ideally wants TTL control per-prefix.

One ask
- Can you provide a very rough order-of-magnitude committed monthly spend for Redwood Dedicated (GPU-backed) options so we can prepare procurement questions? Not looking for final pricing, just a ballpark for our finance leadership so they know if this is enterprise scale.

Availability
- The proposed time for Tue 28 Apr works for Alex and me. We'll add a calendar invite.

Thanks — will push the anonymized datasets by EOD tomorrow.

— Jenna
Head of Product — Clinical AI | Streamline Health
jenna.harris@streamlinehealth.com
+1 (617) 555-0167

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jenna Harris <jenna.harris@streamlinehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:05:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Streamline Health — inference cost pressure & pilot readout

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Jenna — great to hear the team is aligned on constraints. A few concrete follow-ups from us: 

1) Procurement ballpark
- For Dedicated GPU-backed pools (enterprise reserved): typical monthly committed bands start at ~$60k/mo for a small reserved pool (sustained 100k tokens/s equivalent, rough estimate). We will run a tailored capacity estimate once we see your traffic shape.

2) Pilot artifacts we will deliver
- MAP (Mutual Action Plan) PDF (attached: MAP-Streamline-v1.pdf) with milestones and exit criteria.
- Runbook for the shadow deployment + rollback steps.
- Benchmark report with cost-per-1k-token estimates across batching/quants/caching scenarios.

3) Proposed evaluation metric (please confirm)
- Cost: baseline vs pilot cost-per-1k tokens (target >=60% reduction).
- Latency: p95 under pilot traffic shape (target <250ms).
- Quality: relative drop on your clinical retrieval accuracy <=2%. If you prefer F1 or BLEU for any prompts, send the exact metric and eval harness.

4) Calendar
- I created the invite for Tue 28 Apr 10:00–10:30 PT and included Aditya (solutions engineering) who will lead the benching. If the slot doesn't work ping me and I'll reschedule.

Next immediate step (from you)
- Drop the anonymized traffic slice + 10 prompts to the Drive link I shared (or attach here). Once we have that, Aditya will kick off the micro-benchmark and we’ll share an initial report within 5 business days.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly here.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: MAP-Streamline-v1.pdf
